text: It is narrated from Ubadah ibn al-Samit that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever says, ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone (who has no partner); that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger; that Jesus is the servant of Allah, the son of a woman from among the servants of Allah, His word which He conveyed to Mary (bringing him into being in her by His command), and a spirit from Allah; that Paradise is true and Hell is true,’ Allah will admit him into His Paradise through whichever of the eight gates of Paradise he wishes.”

topic: Faith · Visiting the Sick and the Prayers of the Angels
text: Ali reported that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: “Whoever goes to visit his sick Muslim brother walks (as it were) among the fruits of Paradise until he sits down beside him. When he sits down, mercy envelops him. If his visit is in the morning, seventy thousand angels pray for him and seek forgiveness for him until the evening. If his visit is in the evening, seventy thousand angels pray for him and seek forgiveness for him until the morning.”

topic: Faith · The Holy Quran and Miracles
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “There is no prophet who was not given miracles so that people would believe. What I have been given is the revelation that Allah has revealed to me (the Holy Quran). Because of it, I hope to be the prophet with the most followers on the Day of Resurrection.”

It is narrated from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said once, “Blessed are those who saw me and believed!” And he repeated seven times, “Blessed are those who believed in me without seeing me!”

Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: “… By Allah, in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the believer is like the honeybee: it eats what is good, produces what is good, alights (on good places), and does not break or spoil (the place where it alights).”
source: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, II, 199; Hâkim, Müstedrek , I, 110 (1/76)

text: It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever has these four traits is a complete hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it: when he is entrusted with something, he betrays the trust; when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; and when he quarrels, he deviates from the truth.”

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him), praying for Hasan and Husayn, used to seek refuge in Allah for them with these words: “I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah (His infinite will and decree) from every devil, from every harmful creature, and from every evil eye.” Then he would say, “Your forefather Abraham used to make this supplication for his sons Ishmael and Isaac.”

It is narrated from Aisha that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Responsibility is lifted from three people: from the one who is asleep until he wakes up, from the one afflicted with mental illness until he regains his sanity, and from the child until he reaches puberty.”

Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Allah the Exalted says: I am as My servant thinks of Me. I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself. If he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it…”

Abu Hurairah heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say on one occasion: “What do you think: if a river passed by the door of one of you and he bathed in it five times every day, would any of his dirt remain?” The Companions said, “None of his dirt would remain.” Thereupon the Messenger of Allah said, “That is how the five daily prayers are! Through them Allah wipes away sins.”

topic: Worship · The Rights of a Believer over a Believer
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “A believer has six rights over another believer: he visits him when he is ill, attends his funeral when he dies, accepts his invitation when he invites him, greets him with salam when he meets him, prays for him when he sneezes, and is sincere toward him whether he is present or absent.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The blessed month of Ramadan has come to you. Allah the Exalted has made fasting in this month obligatory upon you. In this month the gates of heaven (Paradise) are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the most rebellious of the devils are chained.”

Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “As long as major sins are avoided, the five daily prayers, Friday until the next Friday, and Ramadan until the next Ramadan are a means of forgiveness for the sins committed between them.”

topic: Good Character · Intention and Its Importance
text: Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Deeds are judged by intentions. Everyone will receive only what he intended. Whoever emigrates for Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is for Allah and His Messenger. And whoever emigrates for some worldly gain he seeks or a woman he wishes to marry, his emigration is for that for which he emigrated.”

Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: “Each of you is a guardian, and each of you is responsible for those in your care. The head of state is a guardian and is responsible for those in his care. The man of the house is a guardian and is responsible for those in his care. The woman of the house is also a guardian and is responsible for those in her care. The servant is also a guardian over his master’s property and is responsible for what is in his care.”

It is narrated from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever leaves this world having worshipped Allah, the One who has no partner, with sincerity, having established the prayer and given the zakat, dies while Allah is pleased with him.”

It is narrated from Ubadah ibn al-Samit that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “Guarantee me six things on your part, and I will guarantee you Paradise: be truthful when you speak, keep your promise when you make one, honor a trust when (something) is entrusted to you, guard your chastity, lower your gaze (from what is forbidden to look at), and restrain your hands (from what is unlawful).”

Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “If you were to rely on Allah as He truly deserves to be relied upon, you would be provided for just as the birds are provided for: they go out in the morning with empty stomachs and return (in the evening) full.”

Anas ibn Malik relates that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: “My son! If you are able to reach the morning and the evening without holding deceit against anyone in your heart, then do so. This is my Sunnah. Whoever keeps my Sunnah alive has loved me, and whoever loves me will be with me in Paradise.”

It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “The merciful are those to whom the Most Merciful (al-Rahman) shows mercy. Show mercy to those on earth, so that those in the heavens will show mercy to you! The ‘rahim’ (the bond of kinship) is a bond (derived) from al-Rahman. Whoever maintains it, Allah maintains His bond with him; and whoever severs it, Allah severs His bond with that person.”

topic: Social Life · Being a Good Person
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “When a Muslim dies and the members of three households among his closest neighbors testify that he was a good person, Allah the Exalted says, ‘I have accepted the testimony of My servants who testified according to what they knew, and I have forgiven what I know (of him).’”

topic: Social Life · Enjoining Good and Forbidding Evil
text: Abu Said al-Khudri heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: “Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it at once with his hand. If he is unable to do so, then with his tongue; and if he is unable to do that, then let him take a stand against it with his heart (and not approve of it). And that is the least that faith requires.”

topic: Social Life · Supporting Those Who Fight in the Way of Allah
text: It is narrated from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever equips a soldier (for battle) to fight in the way of Allah is as though he himself has fought. And whoever looks after the family of a warrior who has gone out to fight in the way of Allah, caring for them well in his absence, is also as though he has fought.”

Humayd says: “I heard from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘Of the servants who die and attain a good rank with Allah, none would wish to return to the world, even if he were given the world and everything in it, except the martyr. Because the martyr sees how exalted the rank of martyrdom is, he longs to return to the world and be martyred once more.’”

Umm Salamah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “When an affliction or something painful befalls any of you, let him say: ‘We belong to Allah and to Him we shall return. O Allah! I seek from You the reward for the affliction that has befallen me; so reward me for it and replace it for me with something better.’”

Hasan ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), the grandson of the Messenger of Allah, said: “The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) taught me this supplication to recite in the Witr prayer: ‘O Allah, guide me among those whom You have guided. Grant me well-being among those to whom You have granted health and well-being. Take me into Your protection among those whom You protect. Bless for me what You have given me. Protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. For You decree, and none can decree over You. The one whom You befriend is never humbled. No imperfection befits You. Our Lord! You are Exalted and Blessed.’”

topic: Faith · Deeds That Lead to Paradise
text: Muadh ibn Jabal relates: We were returning with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) from the expedition of Tabuk. When I saw that he was alone, I said, “O Messenger of Allah! Will you tell me of a deed that will lead me into Paradise?” Thereupon the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “Well done! You have asked about a weighty matter. Yet it is easy for the one for whom Allah makes it easy. You perform the obligatory prayer, you give the obligatory zakat, and you meet Allah without associating anything with Him…”
It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “The evil eye is real. If anything could outstrip destiny, it would be the evil eye…”

topic: Faith · Obedience and Submission to Allah
text: Abdullah ibn Abbas related that one day, while he was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) on the same mount, he said to him: “Young man! I will teach you some words. Be mindful of Allah, and Allah will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will (always) find Him beside you. When you ask, ask of Allah! When you need help, seek help from Allah! Know that if all people gathered together to benefit you, they could not benefit you except as Allah has decreed. And if all people gathered together to harm you, they could not harm you in anything except as Allah has decreed. On this matter the pens have been lifted (the decision has been made) and the pages have dried (the judgment is final).”
source: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, I, 293; Tirmidhi, Sıfatü’l-kıyâme, 59

text: Ibn Umar relates: “One day the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said (to a group among whom I was present), ‘Tell me of a tree that resembles a Muslim: by its Lord’s permission it gives fruit at all times, and its leaves do not fall.’ It occurred to me to say, ‘It is the date palm.’ But since Abu Bakr and Umar were there, I did not think it proper to speak. When they did not speak either, the Messenger of Allah said, ‘It is the date palm.’”

Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “On the Day of Resurrection you will find that the worst of people in the sight of Allah are the two-faced, who come to some people with one face and to others with another face!”

Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Look at those who are below you; do not look at those who are above you. This is more fitting, so that you do not belittle the blessings of Allah (upon you).”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “Charity is due every day for every joint of the body. Helping a person who wants to mount his riding animal, or loading his belongings onto it, is charity. A good word, and every step taken on the way to prayer, is charity. Showing someone the way is charity.”

topic: Worship · Being a Friend of Allah
text: Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Allah the Exalted says: ‘Whoever shows enmity to a wali (friend) of Mine, I declare war on him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. And My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts of worship until I love him. (And when I love him,) I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he grasps, and his foot with which he walks. If he asks of Me, I will surely give him (what he asks). If he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely protect and guard him…’”

It is narrated from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever among you has had the door of supplication opened to him, the doors of mercy have been opened to him. Of all the things Allah is asked for, the most beloved to Him is well-being.” The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) continued: “Supplication benefits against calamity that has befallen and that which has not yet befallen. So, O servants of Allah, hold fast to supplication!”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “When a Muslim (or believing) servant performs ablution and washes his face, every sin he looked at with his eyes leaves his face with the water (or with the last drop of water). When he washes his hands, every sin his hands committed leaves his hands with the water (or with the last drop of water). When he washes his feet, every sin his feet walked toward leaves with the water (or with the last drop of water). In the end, that servant emerges purified of his sins.”

topic: Worship · The Imam, the Congregation and the Rows
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “The imam is there only to be followed, so do not act differently from him (in prayer). When he bows, you bow. When he says, ‘Sami’allahu liman hamidah,’ say, ‘Rabbana laka’l-hamd.’ When he prostrates, you prostrate. When he prays sitting, all of you pray sitting. Keep the rows straight in prayer, for keeping the rows straight is part of the beauty of prayer.”

Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever performs ablution and takes care to do it well, then comes to the Friday prayer and listens attentively and silently (to the sermon), his sins between that Friday and the next, and three days more, are forgiven. And whoever busies himself with the pebbles (on the ground instead of listening to the sermon) has engaged in idle play.”

topic: Good Character · The Recompense of Good and Evil Deeds
text: Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Allah, the Possessor of Might and Majesty, said: ‘When My servant intends to do a good deed but does not do it, (I record) one good deed for him; and when he intends to do an evil deed but does not do it, I do not record it (as a sin). But if he does it, I record one evil deed (sin) against him.’”

Abu Hurairah heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: “Allah divided mercy into one hundred parts. He kept ninety-nine parts with Himself and sent down one part to the earth. It is through this one part (of mercy) that all creatures show mercy to one another, so much so that a mare (as a result of this mercy) lifts her hoof away from her foal (while nursing it), fearing she might step on it and harm it.”

topic: Good Character · Kindness and Strong Character
text: It is narrated by Hudhayfah (ibn al-Yaman) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Do not be people of weak character who say, ‘If people do good, we will do good; and if they do wrong, we will do wrong.’ Rather, make it your habit to repay people with goodness when they do good, and not to wrong them when they do evil.”

topic: Good Character · Being a Key to Good and a Lock against Evil
text: It is narrated from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “There are people who are (as it were) keys to good and locks against evil. And there are others who are keys to evil and locks against good. Blessed are those into whose hands Allah the Exalted has placed the keys of good! And woe to those into whose hands Allah the Exalted has placed the keys of evil!”

It is narrated from Ibn Umar that on the day of the conquest of Mecca the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) addressed the people, saying: “O people! Allah has removed from you the arrogance of the Age of Ignorance and the custom of boasting about ancestors. People are of two kinds: the righteous, God-conscious person who is honored in the sight of Allah, and the sinful, wretched person who is lowly in the sight of Allah. People are the children of Adam, and Allah created Adam from dust…”

It is narrated by Abdullah (ibn Mas’ud) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads (a person) to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A person keeps speaking the truth and holding to truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as ‘truthful’ (siddiq). Beware of lying, for lying leads (a person) to wickedness, and wickedness leads to Hell. A person keeps lying and pursuing falsehood until he is recorded with Allah as ‘a liar’ (kadhdhab).”

topic: Social Life · Treating People with Kindness
text: Abdullah ibn Umar narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Give refuge to whoever seeks refuge with you for the sake of Allah. Give to whoever asks of you for the sake of Allah. Accept the invitation of whoever invites you, and repay whoever does you a kindness. If you cannot find anything with which to repay him, then pray for him until you feel that you have repaid him.”

topic: Social Life · The Good Companion and the Bad Companion
text: It is narrated from Abu Musa that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “The good companion and the bad companion are like one who carries musk and one who blows a blacksmith’s bellows. The one carrying musk will either offer you some, or you will buy (musk) from him, or at least you will enjoy a pleasant scent from him. As for the one blowing the bellows, he will either burn your clothes or you will get a foul smell from him!”

topic: Social Life · State Authority and Justice
text: It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: “State authority is the greatest protector. Injustices are fought through it (that is, through the rule of law), and through it people are protected (from dangers). If those who wield this authority command the fear of Allah and rule with justice, they earn reward for what they do. If they act otherwise, they bear (the burden of) it.”

Abu Said al-Khudri narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, and salt for salt are to be sold in equal amounts and hand to hand. Whoever gives more or takes more has engaged in usury. The one who takes and the one who gives are equal in this.”

Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “O people! Fear Allah (as He deserves) and seek (your provision) in good ways. For no one will die until he has received his provision, even if it is delayed. Fear Allah (as He deserves) and seek (your provision) in good ways. Take what is lawful and leave what is forbidden.”

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah that one day the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) asked, “Do you know who the bankrupt one is?” His Companions said, “Among us, the bankrupt one is the person who has neither money nor property.” Thereupon the Prophet said, “Indeed, the bankrupt one of my community is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting and zakat, but who also comes having insulted this one, slandered that one, consumed the wealth of this one, shed the blood of that one, and beaten another. Then the reward of his good deeds is given to this one and that one. If his good deeds run out before the rights he owes to others are settled, the sins of those he wronged are loaded onto him. Then he is thrown into Hell.”
